name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district, a colonial-era hill station at about 1,500 m elevation known for its pine forests, lakes, markets and mild climate.
facts: Named after the deity U Shyllong
Base for exploring Khasi Hills attractions

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, offering panoramic views of Shillong city, the plateau and distant plains. Sacred site associated with the local deity Lei Shillong.

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong, locally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew. Cascades over mossy rocks amid dense ferns and greenery.
facts: Original Khasi name means three-step waterfall
Named after an elephant-shaped rock destroyed in 1897 earthquake

name: Ward's Lake
description: Artificial lake in central Shillong, locally called Nan Polok, with landscaped gardens, walking paths, boating and a colonial-era bridge. Named after Sir William Ward.
facts: Named after Chief Commissioner Sir William Ward
Popular local picnic and evening spot
Surrounded by gardens and flower beds

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Major museum in Shillong showcasing the cultures, traditions, artefacts, textiles and lifestyles of indigenous communities of Northeast India across 17 galleries.
facts: Located in Mawlai area of Shillong

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Historic town once recorded as the wettest place on Earth, now a major tourism hub famous for waterfalls, limestone caves, living root bridges and dramatic escarpment views over Bangladesh plains.
facts: Base for Nohkalikai, root bridges and caves

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 m, plunging from the Sohra plateau into a turquoise pool. Named after a local legend of a woman named Likai.
facts: Fed by plateau rainfall; turquoise plunge pool

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented waterfall cascading in seven streams over the limestone cliffs near Sohra, creating a dramatic multi-tiered spectacle especially during monsoon.
facts: Also known as Seven Sisters Falls

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Easily accessible limestone cave near Sohra with illuminated chambers, stalactites and stalagmites. One of the most visited caves in Meghalaya.
facts: Popular with families and first-time cavers

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, grown from the aerial roots of Ficus elastica trees over generations by the Khasi people. Requires a steep trek of thousands of steps from Tyrna.

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Village in Pynursla block known as Asia's cleanest village for its community-led sanitation and eco-friendly practices. Features living root bridges, bamboo skywalk and views toward Bangladesh.
facts: Bamboo skywalk and living root bridges

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon and viewpoint near Smit offering sweeping views of deep green valleys and rolling hills. Popular for photography and short treks.

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove (Law Lyngdoh) protected for centuries by the Khasi community. No items may be removed from the forest; home to rare flora, monoliths and traditional ritual sites.
facts: Protected by community taboos for centuries
Rule: nothing may be taken from the forest

name: Kongthong Village (Whistling Village)
description: Remote village famous for its unique whistling language (Jingrwai Iawbei) where residents use melodic tunes to identify each other. Also features living root bridges.
facts: Remote location between Sohra and Pynursla

name: Arwah Cave
description: Limestone cave near Sohra known for fossilized marine shells and fish bones visible in the walls, indicating the area was once under the sea. Accessible with scenic approach.

name: Wei Sawdong Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall near Sohra with emerald pools, accessible via a short forest trek. Less crowded than the major falls and popular for swimming.

name: Mawsynram
description: Village holding the record as one of the wettest places on Earth. Features caves, living root bridges and traditional Khasi culture with fewer tourists than Sohra.
facts: One of the wettest places on Earth
